title: Infusion pumps

parameters.name: Programmed rate
parameters.explanation: The rate is the pump setting that governs how quickly the infusion is delivered. Verify it against the order, drug concentration and selected channel rather than using the displayed number alone.

parameters.name: Volume infused
parameters.explanation: This is the cumulative volume registered by the pump for the channel or counting interval. Check when the counter was cleared and reconcile the value with the infusion record and IV site.

parameters.name: Occlusion and air alarms
parameters.explanation: Occlusion alarms indicate pressure consistent with an obstruction; air alarms indicate detected air in the monitored tubing. Assess the patient and the affected infusion, then use the device-specific pathway before resuming.

safety_concepts.text: Verify programming (dosage, rate, volume) at change of shift, when any change is made to the settings, when a new bag is hung and when new tubing is primed (FDA).
Label pump channels and tubing at the port of entry with the drug or fluid name if the pump does not display it (FDA).
Use the drug library where one exists and respond carefully to alerts rather than silencing them (FDA).

monitoring_concepts.text: For high-risk infusions, watch for signs of over- or under-infusion using other available monitoring (for example cardiac monitoring, pulse oximetry, end-tidal CO2 or glucose readings) alongside the pump itself, and monitor the patient and the infusion per facility protocol; a secondary volume check (such as a time strip or buretrol) can help confirm the expected volume has infused.

escalation_concepts.text: Assess the patient and escalate unresolved alerts, programming discrepancies or suspected over- or under-infusion promptly. For a high-risk infusion, stay with the patient and ask a colleague to obtain a replacement pump. Follow the drug-specific backup plan to manage any interruption safely.

If a pump fails or stops working during a high-risk infusion, stay with and closely monitor the patient while another staff member obtains a working pump; for fluid-sensitive patients, clamp and disconnect the tubing to prevent over-infusion until a replacement pump is obtained. Report problems through facility protocol; events involving possible death or serious injury require following the facility's reporting pathway.
